newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas strengthens with cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas strengthens with cold weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices at Sumas, the western Canadian export point were significantly higher Monday, led by below-freezing temperatures in western Canada and tight supplies on the U.S. West Coast.
Prices for Tuesday delivery at Sumas, Wash., jumped more than 20 cents to the $2.15 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) area early and then $2.40 late, industry sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices regained about five to seven cents to the C$2.05-2.06 per gigajoule (GJ) range, reaching the highest levels of the year.
The AECO market was talked in the C$2.055 per GJ area for December and about C$2.10 for January. Summer prices were heard in the mid-C$1.50s.
With western U.S. storage only about 70 percent full, most buyers were likely reluctant to withdraw gas, market sources said.

At Niagara, the eastern Canadian export point, prices were also up about 20 cents to the low-to-mid $3.20s per mmBtu. Foreasters are calling for below-normal temperatures to return to the eastern U.S. by Thursday.
